parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Electrons, each of mass $m$ and charge $q$, are accelerated from rest in a vacuum through a potential difference $V$.

Derive an expression, in terms of $m$, $q$ and $V$, for the final speed $v$ of the electrons. Explain your working.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Show that the specific charge $\frac{q}{m}$ of the electrons is given by the expression

$$\frac{q}{m} = \frac{2V}{B^2r^2}.$$

Explain your working.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Electrons are accelerated through a potential difference $V$ of $230\text{ V}$. The electrons are injected normally into the magnetic field of flux density $0.38\text{ mT}$. The radius $r$ of the circular orbit of the electrons is $14\text{ cm}$.

Use this information to calculate a value for the specific charge of an electron.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest why the arrangement outlined in (ii), using the same values of $B$ and $V$, is not practical for the determination of the specific charge of $\alpha$-particles.
